This comparison analyzes the utilization of the [[bike1-undervisning-i-inflammatorisk-tarmsygdom|BIKE1 - Undervisning i inflammatorisk tarmsygdom]] teaching code across various Danish hospital departments during a specific reporting period [^src1]. The data captures the volume of patient education sessions registered for inflammatory bowel disease, revealing significant disparities in reporting and implementation among regional and specialized units [^src1]. Nationally, the total number of reported teaching codes across Denmark stands at 308 [^src1].

The clear leaders in registering these educational interventions are SLB Vejle Medicinsk Afdeling, which recorded the highest departmental count with 65 instances, and Aarhus Lever-, Mave- og Tarmsygdomme, which followed closely with 56 [^src1]. Other high-performing departments include EGS Esbjerg Medicinsk område with 41 registrations, Bispebjerg Abdominalcenter K with 40, and Herlev Gastroenheden Kir. Med., overafd. D with 37 [^src1]. Mid-tier reporting is seen at Gødstrup Medicinsk Afdeling (30), Silkeborg Diagnostisk Center Medicin (10), and AAUH Aalborg Med.gastroenterologisk område (8), while Bornholm Medicinsk afdeling and Viborg Medicinsk Afdeling each reported 6 instances [^src1].

Conversely, a substantial portion of the listed departments act as trailers, having registered zero teaching codes during the period [^src1]. This group of 16 departments includes major specialized units such as Rigshospitalet Med. Klinik Mave-, Tarm- og Leversygd., OUH Odense Medicinsk Mave-Tarm Afdeling S, and Nordsjælland Kirurgisk overafdeling, as well as several pediatric and regional medical wards like Hvidovre Børneafdeling, Aarhus Børn og Unge, and HOL Holbæk Medicin [^src1]. 

Additionally, five departments are marked with a "#" symbol rather than a numerical value, acting as outliers that indicate missing data, a failure to report, or an inability to extract the metric for Hvidovre Gastroenterologisk afdeling, SUH Køge Medicin, OUH Odense Børne- og Ungeafdeling H, SLB Kolding Børne- og Ungeafdeling, and Randers Medicinsk Afdeling [^src1]. Because the source document provides only a single snapshot of this data from 2023, no longitudinal trends regarding improvement or decline in code utilization can be established [^src1].
